record.original_question: For every family F of n pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the plane, what is the largest guaranteed size of a subset F' of F that admits a simple alternating path when the connecting segments are allowed to intersect input segments outside F'? In particular, can every such family contain a subset of size on the order of sqrt(n) with this property?

evidence.quote: Given a a family F of n disjoint closed line segments, find a subset of it that admits a simple alternating path.
This bound, however, seems to be far from optimal. We believe that the correct value is O(n 1 2 ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F=\{s_1,\dots,s_n\}$ be a family of $n$ pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the plane. A simple alternating path on a subfamily $F'\subseteq F$ is a non-self-intersecting polygonal path $P$ whose edges can be partitioned into two classes: the "segment edges," which are exactly the segments of $F'$ used in their entirety, and the "connecting edges," which join an endpoint of one segment of $F'$ to an endpoint of another, such that segment edges and connecting edges strictly alternate along $P$ and each segment of $F'$ appears exactly once. The connecting edges are required to be pairwise non-crossing and not to cross any segment of $F'$, but they are allowed to cross segments of $F\setminus F'$.

Let $f(n)$ denote the largest integer $k$ such that every family $F$ of $n$ pairwise disjoint closed line segments in the plane admits a subfamily $F'\subseteq F$ with $|F'|\ge k$ that supports a simple alternating path in the above sense.

(a) Determine the asymptotic order of $f(n)$.

(b) In particular, decide whether $f(n)=\Omega(\sqrt{n})$, i.e., whether every family of $n$ pairwise disjoint closed segments contains a subfamily of size on the order of $\sqrt{n}$ that admits such a simple alternating path.
artifact.status_search_result: The best published lower bound on alternating paths through n disjoint segments is Θ(log n) due to Hoffmann and Tóth (2003), where connecting edges must avoid all input segments. The relaxed variant—where connecting edges may cross segments outside the chosen subset—was conjectured to admit subsets of size Ω(√n). Searches turned up no resolution of this specific subset/√n version; related recent work (e.g., Mulzer et al. on long non-crossing alternating paths on bicolored points, 2020) addresses different settings. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Alternating Paths through Disjoint Line Segments (Hoffmann–Tóth)
status_evidence.snippet: Every segment endpoint visibility graph on n disjoint segments admits an alternating path of length Θ(log n), and this is tight up to constants.
status_evidence.claim: Best known lower bound for the strict (no-crossing) version is Θ(log n); no √n bound is established.

status_evidence.title: Long Alternating Paths Exist (Mulzer et al., SoCG 2020)
status_evidence.snippet: Improves the bound for non-crossing alternating paths on bicolored point sets to (1+ε)n; addresses bicolored points, not segment subsets.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress concerns a different setting (bicolored points), not the subset-of-segments problem allowing crossings of unused segments.
